notes: profesora = female teacher.

sentences.text: Mi profesor de inglés es muy bueno.
sentences.translation: My English teacher is very good.

sentences.text: Los profesores están en una reunión.
sentences.translation: The teachers are in a meeting.

notes: los servicios = the restrooms (Spain).

sentences.text: El servicio es muy bueno aquí.
sentences.translation: The service is very good here.

notes: muchacha = girl, young woman. Similar to chico.

sentences.text: La muchacha vive cerca de aquí.
Tengo una reunión a las tres.
sentences.translation: I have a meeting at three.

sentences.text: Nadie está por encima de la ley.

notes: Masculine despite the -a: el programa.

sentences.translation: They show good programs on Sundays.

notes: Also a university degree: terminar la carrera.

sentences.translation: I finish my degree this year.

sentences.text: Le gustan las carreras de coches.

notes: Same form in singular and plural: el cumpleaños, los cumpleaños.

sentences.text: Mañana es el cumpleaños de mi madre.

notes: A little more formal than bonito or lindo.

sentences.text: Es una de las mejores universidades.
sentences.translation: It's one of the best universities.
Are you coming to my wedding?

notes: sala de espera = waiting room. In many places la sala = the living room.

sentences.text: Espere en la sala de espera.
Las salas del museo están cerradas.

notes: tomar una decisión = to make a decision.

sentences.translation: You have to make hard decisions.

sentences.text: Ya tenemos las cosas necesarias para el viaje.
sentences.translation: We already have the things we need for the trip.

notes: tener prisa = to be in a hurry. ¡Date prisa! = Hurry up!
Almost always in sin embargo = however, nevertheless.

sentences.text: Es caro; sin embargo, lo voy a comprar.
sentences.translation: It's expensive; however, I'm going to buy it.

sentences.text: Estaba cansado y, sin embargo, siguió trabajando.
sentences.translation: He was tired, and yet he kept working.

notes: abuela = grandmother. abuelos = grandparents.

sentences.text: Vamos a casa de la abuela.
Mis abuelos viven en el campo.
sentences.translation: My grandparents live in the country.

notes: el detective, la detective.

sentences.text: Los detectives llegaron por la mañana.
sentences.translation: The detectives arrived in the morning.

notes: Also a form of soler: suelo + infinitive = I usually do something.

sentences.translation: I dropped it on the floor.

sentences.text: No te sientes en el suelo.
Los suelos de la casa son de madera.
sentences.translation: The floors in the house are wooden.

sentences.text: Va a ir a la cárcel.
sentences.translation: He's going to go to jail.

sentences.text: Pasó diez años en la cárcel.
sentences.translation: He spent ten years in prison.
She got out of jail yesterday.

notes: Very common in Latin America for aquí. ¡Ven acá! = Come here!
Usually reflexive: sentarse = to sit down. me siento = I sit down (also 'I feel', from sentir).

sentences.translation: She was sitting in the kitchen.

notes: intentar + infinitive = to try to. intento is also the noun 'attempt'.

sentences.translation: I need a bit of quiet.

notes: ser capaz de = to be able to. In Latin America capaz also means 'maybe'.

sentences.translation: I'm not able to do it.
He's a member of the club.

sentences.text: Vamos a un club esta noche.
sentences.translation: We're going to a club tonight.

sentences.text: Hay muchos clubes en el centro.
sentences.translation: There are lots of clubs downtown.

notes: Me temo que... = I'm afraid that... (polite bad news).
estar de broma = to be joking.

sentences.text: Todos los gobiernos dicen lo mismo.
sentences.translation: All governments say the same thing.

notes: Also 'chamber': cámara frigorífica = cold room. cámara lenta = slow motion.

sentences.translation: There are cameras in the street.

sentences.text: Olvidé mi cámara en el hotel.
sentences.translation: I left my camera at the hotel.

sentences.text: Tengo un dolor de cabeza terrible.

sentences.translation: We open the presents at Christmas.

sentences.text: La gente aquí es muy amable.

notes: Also a noun: un dulce = a sweet, a piece of candy.
ataque al corazón = heart attack.

sentences.translation: There were several attacks last night.

notes: Written with a capital letter. ¡Feliz Navidad! = Merry Christmas!

sentences.translation: What are you doing at Christmas?
I work eight hours a day.

notes: en avión = by plane.

sentences.text: El avión sale a las diez.

notes: Te lo juro = I swear (to you).

sentences.translation: He swore to tell the truth.

gloss: to keep; to maintain; to support
notes: Conjugated like tener: mantengo, mantuve.

sentences.text: Ella mantiene a toda la familia.
Mi abuelo estuvo en el ejército.
sentences.translation: My grandfather was in the army.
The army arrived in the town.

sentences.text: Los dos ejércitos se encontraron en el río.
sentences.translation: The two armies met at the river.

notes: hacer el papel de = to play the role of.

sentences.translation: Do you have paper and a pencil?

sentences.text: Tiene un papel importante en la película.
sentences.translation: She has an important role in the movie.

notes: Funny as in making people laugh.
al principio = at first. a principios de = at the beginning of.

sentences.translation: At first, I didn't like it.

notes: delante de = in front of. Latin America also says adelante.

sentences.text: El coche está delante de la casa.
sentences.translation: The car is in front of the house.

sentences.text: No hables así delante de los niños.
sentences.translation: Don't talk like that in front of the children.
The lieutenant wants to see you.

sentences.text: Mi padre era teniente del ejército.
sentences.translation: My father was an army lieutenant.

notes: pedir un deseo = to make a wish.

sentences.text: Mi único deseo es verte feliz.
sentences.translation: My only wish is to see you happy.

notes: nave espacial = spaceship.

sentences.text: La nave llegó a la luna.

sentences.translation: Let's go back to the ship.

sentences.text: Hay dos naves en el cielo.
sentences.translation: There are two ships in the sky.

notes: Also used for something worthless: es una basura.
estar en contacto = to be in touch.

sentences.translation: He has contacts in the government.

notes: en tren = by train.

sentences.translation: I go to work by train.

notes: Feminine, but el alma (stressed a-).

sentences.text: Te quiero con toda mi alma.
sentences.translation: I love you with all my soul.

notes: ¿Cómo andas? = How are you doing? ¡Anda! = Come on! / Wow! Irregular preterite: anduve.

sentences.text: Me gusta andar por el parque.
sentences.translation: I like walking in the park.
He hangs out with bad people.
I've been very tired these days.
They've been married for twenty years.

sentences.text: Viven tres matrimonios en el edificio.
sentences.translation: Three married couples live in the building.

notes: con locura = like crazy, madly.

sentences.translation: We did a lot of crazy things.

notes: de oro = gold, golden.

sentences.translation: It's worth its weight in gold.

sentences.text: No todo lo que brilla es oro.
sentences.translation: All that glitters is not gold.

notes: Con permiso = Excuse me (to get past someone).

sentences.translation: Do you have permission to be here?

notes: directora = female director. In a school: the principal.

sentences.translation: I want to talk to the manager.

sentences.text: La directora de la escuela es muy amable.
sentences.translation: The school principal is very nice.

notes: en peligro = in danger.

sentences.translation: He knows the dangers of the sea.

gloss: to make happy; to be glad (alegrarse)
notes: Me alegro = I'm glad. Me alegra verte = I'm happy to see you.

sentences.text: Se alegró mucho con la noticia.
sentences.translation: She was very happy about the news.

notes: a la derecha = on the right, to the right. Also the political right.

sentences.text: Es la segunda puerta a la derecha.
sentences.translation: It's the second door on the right.

sentences.text: Mi casa está a tu derecha.
sentences.translation: My house is on your right.

sentences.text: No hay espacio en el coche.
sentences.translation: There's no room in the car.
I need a bit of space.
She wants to travel into space.

notes: un rato = a while. al rato = shortly after.

sentences.text: Hace un rato que se fue.
sentences.translation: He left a little while ago.
We had a good time together.

notes: ¡Salud! = Cheers! (and Bless you! after a sneeze).

sentences.text: Fumar es malo para la salud.
sentences.translation: Smoking is bad for your health.
Why are you all so sad?

notes: maestra = female teacher. Usually a schoolteacher; also a master of a craft.

sentences.text: El maestro nos dio mucha tarea.
sentences.translation: The teacher gave us a lot of homework.

sentences.text: Es un maestro de la cocina.
sentences.translation: He's a master in the kitchen.

notes: según tú = according to you, in your opinion.

sentences.text: Según el médico, no es grave.
sentences.translation: According to the doctor, it's not serious.
In your opinion, who's to blame?

sentences.text: Según el día, voy en tren o en coche.
sentences.translation: Depending on the day, I go by train or by car.

notes: Plural with an accent: crímenes.

sentences.text: ¿Dónde estaba en el momento del crimen?
sentences.translation: Where were you at the time of the crime?

sentences.text: Hay pocos crímenes en este pueblo.
sentences.translation: There are few crimes in this town.

notes: un consejo = a piece of advice. consejos = advice.

sentences.translation: Can you give me some advice?

gloss: before; in front of; faced with
notes: Formal. ante todo = above all, first of all.

sentences.translation: First of all, thank you for coming.

sentences.text: Todos somos iguales ante la ley.
sentences.translation: We're all equal before the law.

sentences.text: No sé qué hacer ante esta situación.
sentences.translation: I don't know what to do in this situation.

sentences.text: Vamos a la iglesia los domingos.
sentences.translation: We go to church on Sundays.

sentences.text: La boda es en la iglesia del pueblo.
sentences.translation: The wedding is in the village church.

sentences.text: Hay muchas iglesias en esta ciudad.
sentences.translation: There are many churches in this city.

notes: la mayoría de = most (of).

sentences.text: La mayoría de la gente está de acuerdo.
La mayoría de mis amigos viven aquí.
sentences.translation: Most of my friends live here.

notes: hacer una escena = to make a scene.

sentences.text: Cortaron dos escenas de la película.
sentences.translation: They cut two scenes from the movie.

notes: In Spain piso = apartment, flat. In Latin America: departamento or apartamento.

sentences.translation: I live on the third floor.

sentences.text: Busco un piso en el centro.
sentences.translation: I'm looking for an apartment downtown.
It's an honor to meet you.

notes: Irregular past participle: abierto.

sentences.text: La tienda abre a las nueve.

sentences.translation: He's the brains of the group.

notes: preguntar = ask a question; pedir = ask for something. me pregunto = I wonder.
Also a cuisine (la cocina italiana) and a stove.

sentences.text: Las cocinas de estos pisos son pequeñas.
sentences.translation: The kitchens in these apartments are small.

notes: Also the past participle of vestir: vestido de negro = dressed in black.

sentences.text: Me voy a poner el vestido rojo.
sentences.translation: I'm going to wear the red dress.

notes: montar a caballo = to ride a horse.
In Spain a bar is also a café where people eat and drink coffee.

sentences.text: Hay un bar en la esquina.
sentences.translation: There's a bar on the corner.
We went out to bars last night.

notes: Mostly Latin America; Spain prefers dentro.

sentences.text: Los niños juegan adentro cuando llueve.
sentences.translation: The kids play inside when it rains.

notes: Means illegal drugs. Medicine is medicamento.
Also written en seguida.

sentences.translation: It was a very pleasant afternoon.
Do you prefer meat or fish?

sentences.text: En esta tienda venden carnes muy buenas.
sentences.translation: This shop sells very good meats.

notes: In much of Latin America departamento = apartment.

sentences.text: Trabaja en el departamento de ventas.
sentences.translation: She works in the sales department.
I live in a small apartment.

sentences.text: Hay departamentos libres en este edificio.
sentences.translation: There are vacant apartments in this building.
